title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-04-06
lineage: SBD > FM > MR > C > D > CD

ai_review.summary: A rough‑but‑listenable soundboard captures a manic 1969 Avalon show highlighted by an explosive Viola Lee Blues and a fire‑filled The Other One.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its high‑octane, psychedelic energy – Baby Blue, Death Don't Have No Mercy, King Bee and especially the legendary Viola Lee Blues with its power‑outage ending make this a fan favorite.  The recording is a soundboard tape that suffers from high‑frequency distortion, occasional drop‑outs and a two‑minute guitar silence, but it remains sharp enough to enjoy the historic jams.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4–5 stars and highlight its intense performance; recording issues are noted but not enough to outweigh the musical strengths, yielding a weighted rating around 4.2.

recording_quality.technical_notes: High‑frequency distortion, occasional drop‑outs (e.g., Garcia’s guitar cuts out for ~2 min), power outage noise at the end of Viola Lee Blues; overall sharp but not balanced or pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑Dead set with extended jams; the show builds into a wild, manic climax highlighted by Viola Lee Blues and The Other One suite.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar briefly cuts out during Viola Lee Blues but his vocals are solid throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Hot, sweet organ work on Viola Lee Blues (likely Pig Pen) praised by several listeners.
